topics.topic: Which processes or tasks process_count includes and how the configured count maps to simultaneous processes
questions: Does `process_count` bound all processes in the execution including the runner, or only additional processes created by the implementation, and therefore exactly how many simultaneous processes must be permitted?
Does `process_count` limit child processes only, all processes including the runner, or all tasks counted by `RLIMIT_NPROC`, including threads?
Does process_count bound all processes in the execution including the runner, or processes created by user code in addition to the runner, and which sandbox helper or namespace-init processes count?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] The parent MUST enforce bounds from outside: address space limited to bounds.memory_bytes with setrlimit and the size of a file written in the scratch with setrlimit, the only limits the parent sets; the outer process bound is the setrlimit limit on the number of processes at bounds.process_count + 1, set by the runner inside the sandbox's user namespace before it loads the code — the one is the task bubblewrap's init would be, and with the runner as the namespace's init it is the margin that keeps the outer bound above the audit hook's exact count; set by the parent, that limit would count every process of the user on the host and bubblewrap could not create its namespace (EAGAIN) — process_count itself being enforced by the runner's audit hook, a wall deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken when the environment starts plus bounds.wall_time_ms in nanoseconds and held in a local variable of execute_function only, after which — once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it — it kills every process of the environment by sending SIGKILL, through a pidfd, to the environment's PID-namespace init, the child-pid bubblewrap reports on --info-fd — not to bubblewrap itself or its process group — and then waits for bubblewrap to exit, and an output count, the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the runner's limit on the number of processes, process_count + 1, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
judgement.why: State 8 explicitly defines which tasks count, identifies the runner as the first task, excludes bubblewrap, and explains the additional outer-limit margin.

topics.topic: Outcome when the runner fails to install a resource limit before loading user code
questions: What happens if an individual execution's runner cannot install the process limit before loading the module?
Must the execution be refused before code loads, classified as a particular execution outcome, or stop the kernel when either setrlimit operation fails?

quotes: ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` — address space by the parent, from outside the environment; the process count by the runner inside the environment's user namespace before the code loads, at `process_count` plus one, since a process limit set by the parent counts every process of the kernel's user on the host and the namespace could not be created (decision 30, 2026-10-11) — and the parent's own wall deadline and output count.

Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised — `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the process exited abnormally — `crashed`; the returned dict does not have exactly the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema, or a file output is not `bytes` — `contract_violation`; otherwise the execution succeeded.

The kernel checks at start, before recovery and before the surface opens, that `bubblewrap` is present and that one probe execution succeeds; without both it does not start, and says why. A running kernel therefore always has a sandbox.
judgement.divergence: One implementation classifies failure to install either limit as a `crashed` execution and continues serving; another reports `resource_exhausted`, refuses the execution before loading code, or stops the kernel, which the caller notices in the execution outcome and continued availability.
judgement.why: The rules require both limits and give an outcome order, but do not map failure of either limit-installation operation to an outcome or kernel-lifecycle action.

topics.topic: Required UID isolation, capabilities, baseline, and soft/hard limits for enforcing process_count
questions: What user-ID mapping, capability state and process baseline must the sandbox establish so that the in-namespace process limit counts only this execution and is actually enforced against its code?
What exact soft limit, hard limit, UID mapping and capability state must the runner establish so untrusted code cannot raise or bypass the process limit?

quotes: Every function execution, in trial and in a run alike, runs in a fresh isolated environment created by the sandbox: Linux `bubblewrap` with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces, no network interface but the namespace's own loopback — up, as bubblewrap leaves it in a new network namespace, and reaching nothing outside the execution, so K-02's "no network" holds; this is a property of how the kernel starts bubblewrap, which the kernel does not inspect or verify at run time — the start check (rule 8) asks only that a probe execution succeeds — an environment holding only `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (rule 2), a read-only runtime, and one private exchange directory bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`.

ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` — address space by the parent, from outside the environment; the process count by the runner inside the environment's user namespace before the code loads, at `process_count` plus one, since a process limit set by the parent counts every process of the kernel's user on the host and the namespace could not be created (decision 30, 2026-10-11) — and the parent's own wall deadline and output count.
judgement.divergence: One implementation installs both soft and hard limits and removes every capability that could bypass or raise them under a private UID mapping; another installs only a soft limit or retains an exempt capability or shared counted UID, allowing agent code to raise or bypass the bound or causing unrelated tasks to consume it, which the owner notices as excess processes or differing `resource_exhausted` outcomes.
judgement.why: Neither State 2 nor the later texts fix the soft and hard limit values, UID mapping, or capability state needed to make the stated outer process bound non-bypassable.

topics.topic: Status precedence between skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed when inputs have mixed causes
questions: When one input port is unreachable through guards or skipped nodes while another input comes from a failed or `upstream_failed` node, is the node recorded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`?
When one input port is unreachable by guards or skipped sources and another input comes from a failed node, which status must be recorded?

quotes: A node an input of which comes from a failed node, or from a node itself `upstream_failed`, concludes `upstream_failed` without executing; when both rule 4 and this rule apply, this rule wins.
judgement.why: A13 explicitly gives `upstream_failed` precedence when the guard-skip and upstream-failure conditions both apply.

topics.topic: What constant composition carries and when StoredValue creation or reuse assigns value_id
questions: Does composition receive literal bytes/value plus schema and class and compute/store the `value_id`, or does it receive a reference to an existing StoredValue?
What does the compose request carry for a constant, and at what point does the kernel create or reuse the StoredValue and place its generated value_id in the FlowConstant?

quotes: A flow constant is a typed literal (M16): the composing agent declares its `value_schema` with its class, and its StoredValue takes both.
Writing a StoredValue whose `value_id` exists returns the existing record; repeating any other immutable record is `StoreInternalError`, since its caller checks existence first.

handle_compose_flow_version: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST turn each RequestConstant into a ConstantInput with the same to_node, to_port, canonical value_schema text and disclosure_class and with canonical_json set to the canonical bytes of its json_text.

handle_compose_flow_version: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call compose_flow_version with the flow_id, purpose, inputs, outputs, nodes, edges, the converted constants and the actor, and show the composed version's constants to the actor, each FlowConstant value being the value_id of a StoredValue shown through show_port_refs.
judgement.why: The later contracts and notes make the request carry a literal JSON value, schema, and class, have composition create or reuse its StoredValue, and place the resulting generated value_id in the FlowConstant.

topics.topic: Whether empty node_id is reserved for flow endpoints and how endpoint identity is represented
questions: Is the empty string reserved exclusively for flow endpoints, or how is a node with `node_id == ""` distinguished from them?
May a flow node have node_id equal to the empty string, and if so how is it distinguished from a flow endpoint?

quotes: - `from_node`, `from_port`: a node's output port or a flow input;
- `to_node`, `to_port`: a node's input port or a flow output; a flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node (A05 rule 2), never the `flow_id`;

Composition refuses, before anything is kept, a flow version whose node ids repeat, whose flow input or output port names repeat within a direction, or which declares a flow input or output of `file` carriage (M13), a flow input without a class, or a flow output with one (M01), or a constant whose value does not fit the schema declared with it (M16) — the first of these, in this order, is named; a kept constant is therefore always a validated StoredValue (M21); the proof never sees such a version.
judgement.divergence: One implementation reserves `""` and refuses a FlowNode with that `node_id`; another accepts it and then treats an edge endpoint carrying `from_node` or `to_node` equal to `""` either as that node or as a flow endpoint, which the composing agent notices in proof results and the caller notices in run routing.
judgement.why: The texts assign the empty node identifier to flow endpoints but forbid only repeated node identifiers, leaving an observable namespace collision unresolved.

topics.topic: Whether a denied process creation forces resource_exhausted and how the limit hit is reported
questions: Does an attempted process creation denied by the limit always make the execution resource_exhausted, even when the implementation catches the error, and how must that hit be communicated to the parent?

topics.topic: Whether constant-fed ports participate in the guard skip test
questions: Is the skip test restricted to an unfilled port whose declared edge sources have all become unavailable, so a constant-fed port never causes a skip?

topics.topic: Which process memory_bytes limits, when it is installed, and whether pre-load memory counts
questions: Exactly which process is limited, when is the limit installed, and does memory consumed before user code loads count against memory_bytes?
